messages.subject: Variance contraints
parts:
Dear all,

 

I have questions regarding variance constraints when one fixes the variance of a latent variable to 1. Depending on the type of model (bifactor and second-order model) I am asking if it is the total variance or only the residual variance that is constrained to 1. 

 

In the second-order model if I add the following constraints (S1 ~~ 1*S1 S2 ~~ 1*S2 S3 ~~ 1*S3) what is really constrained? Is it the residual variance of the first-order factors or the total variance ?

 

I have the same question regarding the bifactor model where there is no first-order factors ?

 

Thanks in advance for your help

 

 

Hereunder are my syntaxes for a bifactor as well as a second-order model. I have two questions :

 

model_bif <- '

 

g  =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6 + y7 + y8 + y9

S1 =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3

S2 =~ NA*y4 + y5 + y6

S3 =~ NA*y7 + y8 + y9

 

S1 + S2 + S3 ~~ 0*g

S1 + S2 ~~ 0*S3

S1 ~~ 0*S2

 

g  ~~ 1*g

S1 ~~ 1*S1

S2 ~~ 1*S2

S3 ~~ 1*S3'

 

model_sec <- '

 

S1 =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3

S2 =~ NA*y4 + y5 + y6

S3 =~ NA*y7 + y8 + y9

g_f =~ NA*S1 + S2 + S3 

 

S1 + S2 + S3 ~~ 0*g_f

S1 + S2 ~~ 0*S3

S1 ~~ 0*S2

 

g_f ~~ 1*g_f

S1 ~~ 1*S1

S2 ~~ 1*S2

S3 ~~ 1*S3'

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Variance contraints
parts:
The creators of lavaan made the choice to standardize the residual variances of the factors rather than standardizing the factors' total variance. Residual variances are parameters of the model, while total variances are not, if the factors are dependent on predictors.
      If you want to force factor total variances to be standardized, you can do that with constraints. If your structural model is:

factor1 = b2 * factor2 + error

then the total variance of factor1 is (assuming predictor and error are orthogonal):

variance (factor1) = b2 squared * variance (factor2) + variance(error)

So if you want the total variance of factor1 to be 1, you can constrain the error variance to be 1 - the variance accounted for by the predictor. So label error variance parameters and specify a constraint:

factor1 ~ b2*factor2
factor1 ~~ a*factor1
factor2 ~~ c*factor2
a == 1 - (b2^2) * c

If factor2 here is itself standardized and without predictors, then its (total) variance is 1, and this code simplifies to:

factor1 ~ b2*factor2
factor1 ~~ a*factor1
a == 1 - b2^2

parts:
Dear Edward,

Thank ou very much for your helpful reply. I have question linked to this aspect. 

When I delete freeing the first loading of each first observed variable with NA* and also delete fixing all variances to 1 g  ~~ 1*g S1 ~~ 1*S1 S2 ~~ 1*S2 S3 ~~ 1*S3 I got in the output of all my unstandardized loadings at 1.

I am asking why given that normally Lavaan contraints only the loading of the first observed variable to one.

But I am asking if it is not linked to my covmat as input given that all my variances are 1.

Can you help me wit this issue ?

Many thanks in advance.

lower <- '
1
0.74  1
0.74 0.74  1
0.49 0.49 0.49 1
0.49 0.49 0.49 0.74 1
0.49 0.49 0.49 0.74 0.74 1
0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 1
0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.74 1
0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.74 0.74 1

'

model.cov <-
  getCov(lower, names = c("y1", "y2",
                          "y3", "y4",
                          "y5", "y6","y7", "y8","y9"))

model_bif <- '

g  =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6 + y7 + y8 + y9
S1 =~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3
S2 =~ NA*y4 + y5 + y6
S3 =~ NA*y7 + y8 + y9

S1 + S2 + S3 ~~ 0*g
S1 + S2 ~~ 0*S3
S1 ~~ 0*S2

g  ~~ 1*g
S1 ~~ 1*S1
S2 ~~ 1*S2
S3 ~~ 1*S3'

fit_bifactor <- sem(model_bif,
           sample.cov = model.cov,
           sample.nobs = 2000)
summary(fit_bifactor, fit.measures =TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Variance contraints
parts:
I would guess that those loadings of 1 are starting values only, not maximum likelihood estimates. Starting values of 1 are plausible, but you could set other starting values using the start() modifier or the ? operator. You could change some starting values are demonstrate for yourself that this is happening.

The output should come with a warning that standard errors could not be estimated and that the model is not statistically identified. The common factor model is inherently not identified without constraints. (Pretty much every statistical model has such required constraints.) To achieve identification for a factor model, the typical approaches are (1) fix one loading per factor to a nonzero value--1 for convenience, (2) fix each factors variance or residual variance to a nonzero value--again, 1 for convenience, or (30 in the "effects coding" approach, constrain the average loading for each factor to 1.
